Organ workstations: meshes simplified only where every original vertex stays within 1 mm

items: All 418 quotes were found word for word on the live openstax.org pages, and all 22 section links open the right page and paragraph.
All 2,234 meshes in the dataset exist in the official archive, and every name and FMA ID matches the official tables.
The 3D geometry is read straight from the official archive (isa_BP3D_4.0_obj_99.zip). In every organ and bone workstation, every vertex of the original lies within 1.0 mm of what you see.
The data errors listed in each organ's Notes tab (two misplaced lung arteries, two brain structures named for the wrong side) are present in the official archive itself.

Female body: every Human Reference Atlas model used has a CC BY 4.0 licence and a DOI in its own metadata. In the female reproductive and pelvis workstations, every vertex of the original lies within 0.9 mm of what you see (files pinned by SHA-256, ccf-releases commit b036a91).

The official archive has five pairs of meshes with the same FMA ID and identical geometry (hyoid bone FJ2772/FJ3201, cricoid cartilage FJ2440/FJ2769, celiac artery FJ1846/FJ2013, hepatic artery FJ1916/FJ2386 and FJ1924/FJ2394). Only the first mesh of each pair is shown.

Allen_F_Brain.glb.title: 3D Reference Organ for Brain, Female v1.2
Allen_F_Brain.glb.description: This reference organ was created using data from the "Allen Human Reference Atlas – 3D, 2020" representing one half of the human brain (Ding et al., 2016). The 141 anatomical structures were mirrored to arrive at a whole human brain (as intended) and resized to fit the Visible Human Male and Female bodies. Note that this organ is not licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Instead, these terms of use apply: Allen Institute Terms of Use.

crosscheck.name: WebMD
crosscheck.use: Used only to cross-check facts. No WebMD text, image or model is copied into the app; the summaries below are our own words.

items.ours: The human heart consists of four chambers: The left side and the right side each have one atrium and one ventricle.

page.title: Heart Anatomy, Function, and Blood Circulation

items.summary: WebMD also lists two atria and two ventricles, with a wall (the septum) dividing the left and right sides.

items.ours: A typical heart is approximately the size of your fist: 12 cm (5 in) in length, 8 cm (3.5 in) wide, and 6 cm (2.5 in) in thickness.

page.title: Heart Anatomy, Function, and Blood Circulation

items.summary: WebMD also describes the heart as fist-sized. It gives no measurements, so the centimetre figures are not cross-checked.

items.ours: The right lung consists of three lobes: the superior, middle, and inferior lobes. The left lung consists of two lobes: the superior and inferior lobes.

page.title: Lobectomy Lung Surgery: Purpose, Procedure, and Recovery

items.summary: WebMD gives five lobes in all: three in the right lung and two in the left.

items.ours: The longest part of the alimentary canal, the small intestine is about 3.05 meters (10 feet) long in a living person (but about twice as long in a cadaver due to the loss of muscle tone).
items.summary: WebMD says that, spread out, the small intestine would be more than 20 feet long. That is about twice the OpenStax figure for a living person and close to its figure for a cadaver. The two sources measure different things, so the app keeps the OpenStax sentence, which states both. Both agree that the small intestine has three parts: duodenum, jejunum and ileum.

items.ours: The gallbladder is 8–10 cm (~3–4 in) long and is nested in a shallow area on the posterior aspect of the right lobe of the liver.

page.title: Gall Bladder Pain: Causes, Symptoms, Treatment

items.summary: WebMD also places the gallbladder below the liver and describes it as small and pear-shaped. It gives no length.

items.ours: One of the original regions of the embryonic brain, the midbrain is a small region between the thalamus and pons.

page.title: Brainstem: Function, Location, Health Problems, and More

items.summary: WebMD lists the brainstem from top to bottom as midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata, with the medulla joining the spinal cord.

items.ours: The skull workstation has 8 brain-case meshes (frontal, occipital, sphenoid, ethmoid, two parietal, two temporal) and 14 facial-bone meshes (two each of maxilla, palatine, zygomatic, nasal, lacrimal and inferior nasal concha, plus the vomer and mandible).

page.title: The Skull: Function, Composition, Health Problems, and More

items.summary: WebMD counts 22 skull bones and names the same 14 facial bones. So the dataset's skull is complete at the level of whole bones: 8 + 14 = 22.
